statement: You are given a binary tree whose values may be negative. The tree is given as the array tree in level order, indexed from 0: the root is tree[0], and the left and right children of the node at index i are at indices 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. null marks a position with no node, and every position below a null must be null too.

A path is a sequence of nodes in which each pair of neighbours is joined by an edge, and no node appears more than once. A path holds at least one node and does not need to pass through the root. Its path sum is the sum of the values of its nodes.
Return the largest path sum over all non-empty paths.

examples.explanation: The path 2 → 1 → 3 uses every node, and its sum 2 + 1 + 3 = 6 is the largest.
The best path, 15 → 20 → 7, sums to 42. Extending it through the root would add -10, so the root is left out.
A path must contain at least one node, so the only path is the root by itself, with sum -3.
